quīvis-cumque , quaeviscumque, quodviscumque,
I.pron. indef., who or what you please, any whatsoever you will, each, every (poet.): “nec repentis itum cujusviscumque animantis Sentimus,” Lucr. 3, 388 : “quoviscumque loco potes,” at whatever place you please, Mart. 14, 1, 13 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
